$schema: A location is a place on the storybook map. x/y are 0..1 fractions of the world canvas. glyph drives the procedural illustration. palette tints the local glow.

locations.name: The Moon Pond
locations.blurb: A still black mirror that only ever shows the moon, even at noon. Selkies come here to remember the shape of the sea.
locations.lore: Holy and haunted wells dot the Irish landscape; their reflective stillness was said to be a thin place where the Otherworld pressed close.

locations.name: The Fairy Mound
locations.blurb: A green hill that hums on quiet evenings. Beneath it lies a hall longer than the hill is wide.
locations.lore: A sídhe (shee) is a fairy mound — often a neolithic passage tomb. The Aos Sí, 'the people of the mounds', were thought to live within.

locations.name: The Stone Circle
locations.blurb: Nine grey sentinels keeping a count no one living remembers. The grass inside them never frosts.
locations.lore: Ireland's stone circles, like Drombeg in Cork, are aligned to the turning year. Folklore made them dancers turned to stone for revelling on the Sabbath.

locations.name: The Mist Gate
locations.blurb: Where the fog stands up like a doorway. Step through on the wrong evening and you come out a hundred years late.
locations.lore: The veil between worlds was thinnest at thresholds and at Samhain. Travellers feared the 'stray sod' that turned a known path strange.

locations.name: The Glowing Kelp Grove
locations.blurb: A drowned forest of light just under the tide. The Merrow tend it like a garden of green lamps.
locations.lore: Beneath the waves lay Tír fo Thuinn, the 'Land under Wave' — one of many names for the Irish Otherworld, as real as any island.
